CATALYTIC BIRTH COALESCENCE, FINITE BALANCED FORESTS AND GLOBAL COSTS
ROOT mathematical derivation, 11 November 2026

1. The exact remaining universal contract

Retain arbitrary original species dimension d and expanded reaction order D,
exact original activities/detailed balance, the global supplied drift LN<=A,
canonical zero auxiliaries/nonzero integer decoder, exact all-state directed
classes, elementary arity on both sides, complete timed/null/parallel labelled
paths, all independent predictable fine coefficient faults and universal
polynomial binary and physical costs. Actual all-time population and ALL-firing
costs include untruncated rare paths. They require linear/quadratic growth in
physical time, not necessarily a time-uniform bounded mean.

P3_889E4D_UI_COPIED_FULL_FINAL_20261111.md constructs the full scalar theorem
with variable D. A rare reversible forest on all binary fine complexes pays
negative quadratic drift with exact activities and inverse-polynomial fault
margins. The scalar payload dictionary closes; arbitrary vector closure is not
proved. Its unaugmented 2X<->3X linear-potential obstruction concerns that
topology, not all permitted designs. The following construction addresses a
genuinely mixed-support two-species example using a different occupancy charge.

2. A finite dictionary obstruction for the UNIT occupancy surcharge

Consider the admitted original network
  A+B <-> 2A+B,  0 <-> B,
with unit rates/activities, omega=(1,1), and original upper drift
  LN(a,b)=1-b(a-1)^2<=1.
For any finite nonzero integer payload dictionary containing original A, let S
be a species with largest PURE A payload K A. Such a species exists. Put
  V_1(z)=sum_s (1+|P_s|_1)z_s.
At the binary complex 2S, no admissible elementary edge can strictly decrease
V_1. A hidden target must have payload 2K A; it cannot be unary by maximality
of K, and a binary hidden target has the same V_1. None of the three nonempty
original labels is enabled at pure A payload. The enabled original birth
0->B has target payload 2K A+B; its target has at least one molecule, hence
V_1(target)>=1+(2K+1)=V_1(2S). Empty targets cannot have that payload.

Thus the scalar prescription with surcharge ONE cannot give a strictly
descending parent to every binary vertex, no matter how its finite dictionary
is enlarged. This is a proof about that potential/parent class, not a universal
